claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my child. I have one child - Alex, who is 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether they are in approved education or training. You can normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and stays in approved education or training.

Could you please tell me if Alex is currently in approved education or training (such as A-levels, a BTEC, or other similar qualifications)? Or have they left education/training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. He's studying for his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming that Alex is studying for his A-levels. A-levels count as approved education, so that's a positive sign for eligibility.

I have a few more questions to check the other eligibility criteria:

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! That's helpful to know.

Now, regarding your responsibility for Alex:

Does Alex live with you, or if not, do you contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount (currently £25.60 per week for an eldest/only child) towards their upkeep - for example on food, clothes, or pocket money?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to complete the eligibility check:

Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or started receiving any benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's just focused on his A-levels at the moment. And he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that information.

One final question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all the information I needed. Based on what you've told me, I can now assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why you qualify:

- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ Alex lives with you, making you responsible for him
- ✅ Although Alex is 18, he is under 20 and in approved education (A-levels)
- ✅ Alex is not working 24+ hours per week
- ✅ Alex is not receiving benefits in his own name
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You can apply for Child Benefit through the official government channels. Please note that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay a High Income Child Benefit Tax Charge, but you can still claim and choose whether to receive the payments.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
